**Summary**


What smart home solutions are reshaping modern residential construction? JD Wix outlines how connected thermostats, indoor-air-quality insights, water leak prevention, and smart safety systems help builders meet energy standards, improve energy efficiency, and deliver long-term value for homeowners.


# The connected comfort movement: Integrating smart HVAC, safety, and water solutions for energy efficient homes


## Honeywell Home products and First Alert solutions from Resideo help builders design smart, safe, and efficient homes

9/02/26


By: JD Wix, Senior Director, Vertical Markets at Resideo


As homes become more connected, the conversation around energy efficiency is expanding beyond insulation, solar panels, and building envelopes. Today’s high-performance homes rely on intelligent systems that not only conserve resources but also help make everyday living safer and more efficient.


Resideo Technologies, Inc., through its trusted Honeywell Home® and First Alert® brands, is helping builders deliver that future – one where energy management, water conservation, and life safety technologies work together in harmony. From thermostats that anticipate homeowners’ energy needs, to sensors that stop water leaks before damage occurs, these innovations are helping shape the future of eco-friendly, smart construction.


## Smart energy management: Comfort that saves


Heating and cooling account for roughly half of a home’s total energy consumption, making HVAC systems an extremely powerful lever for efficiency gains. For single-family home builders aiming to meet energy-code requirements and exceed buyer expectations, and for multifamily developers looking to manage comfort and energy use across multiple units, the family of Honeywell Home smart thermostats and whole-home humidity control solutions offer scalable options that support sustainability goals and everyday comfort.


The[Honeywell Home FocusPRO® S200 Smart Thermostat](https://www.resideo.com/us/en/pro/products/air/thermostats/wifi-thermostats/focuspror-s200-smart-thermostat-3h-2c-heat-pump-2h-2c-conventional-th2320wf4010-u/) delivers energy-saving benefits in a simple, affordable design. It allows builders to offer programmable or smart options within the same platform – ideal for entry-level or multifamily projects.


For a premium, contractor-focused option, the new[Honeywell Home ElitePRO™ S1200 Smart Thermostat](https://www.honeywellhome.com/products/elitepro-s1200-smart-thermostat) , powered by[Pro-IQ™ services](https://www.resideo.com/us/en/pro/proiq/) , delivers advanced comfort control, intelligent energy insights and preventative maintenance features that help reduce unnecessary HVAC service visits. Its ENERGY STAR® certification and integrated indoor air quality (IAQ) monitoring support energy efficiency. Monthly energy use reports and guided setpoints are also available to help homeowners achieve additional energy savings.


Honeywell Home ElitePRO smart thermostat


Honeywell Home thermostat users can save on energy consumption when using the recommended scheduling feature consistently. For builders, those savings can translate to improved HERS scores and increased buyer appeal. Energy efficiency is not just a sustainability metric; it’s a key driver of both comfort and long-term cost savings, and providing flexible, connected solutions allows builders to meet a wide range of project needs.


As homes become better insulated and more tightly sealed, managing indoor humidity is becoming an increasingly important part of overall HVAC performance. Excess indoor moisture can make homes feel less comfortable, increase cooling demand and contribute to long-term moisture-related issues. The[Honeywell Home Whole Home Dehumidifier](https://www.resideo.com/us/en/pro/whole-home-dehumidifier/) works alongside the home's HVAC system to help maintain balanced indoor humidity, improve comfort, support HVAC efficiency, and reduce the risk of moisture-related issues.


## Fire and CO safety for modern homes


Life safety is another critical area where smart home technology can help enhance awareness and response. As modern homes incorporate more synthetic materials and open-concept designs, fires burn hotter and spread faster, making early detection essential.


The[First Alert SC5 Smart Smoke and Carbon Monoxide (CO) Alarm](https://www.firstalert.com/products/sc5-battery-smart-smoke-carbon-monoxide-alarm) includes Precision Detection™ Technology, which offers early warning while reducing nuisance alarms caused by cooking smoke or steam – one of the most common reasons homeowners disable their detectors.


These devices also can be interconnected, so when one alarm sounds, all compatible alarms activate throughout the home. Alerts are instantly delivered to homeowners on the mobile app, notifying them whether they are at home or away.


First Alert SC5 Smart Smoke and CO Alarm


For builders focused on occupant safety and building performance, integrating smart fire and CO alarms demonstrates a commitment not just to code compliance, but to resilience and occupant well-being.


## Water conservation and detection: Preventing loss before it happens


While fire often captures headlines, water damage remains the most common – and most expensive – home insurance claim. Issues like frozen pipes, undetected leaks, and excess humidity can lead to thousands of dollars in repairs. The[First Alert L-Series Water Leak Detection and Prevention](https://www.firstalert.com/collections/water-products) solutions give builders a way to help homeowners mitigate these risks from the moment they move in.


At the center of the portfolio is the[First Alert L5 WiFi Water Leak Shutoff Valve](https://www.firstalert.com/products/l5-wifi-water-leak-shutoff-valve?) , which automatically closes the home’s main water line when a leak is detected, preventing widespread damage. Complementary devices such as the[First Alert L1 WiFi Water Leak and Freeze Detector](https://www.firstalert.com/products/l1-wifi-water-leak-freeze-detector?variant=51390590124306) monitor basements, laundry rooms, and mechanical areas for early signs of leaks, freezing temperatures, or elevated humidity – alerting homeowners before a small issue becomes a costly event.


Collectively, these leak detection products have helped consumers save millions of gallons of water and avoid millions in potential insurance claims. For homeowners, that means fewer emergencies and more confidence in their home. For builders, it becomes a tangible demonstration of environmental stewardship – reducing water waste, minimizing unexpected repairs, and contributing to long-term sustainability goals by identifying problems before they start.


First Alert L5 WiFi Water Leak Shutoff Valve


## Unifying smart home control through one app


As these intelligent systems multiply across the home, simplicity becomes just as important as performance. The evolution of the[Total Connect 2.0](https://www.resideo.com/us/en/total-connect-app/) app from Resideo brings together air, water, and safety management into a single intuitive platform. Homeowners can now manage their thermostats, alarms, cameras, and leak detectors from one place – helping reduce app fatigue and simplifying system setup for builders.


For sustainability-minded builders, unified control means fewer standalone systems to integrate and maintain, ensuring the home’s intelligent features work together to deliver measurable efficiency gains.


The app’s growing ecosystem also integrates with smart locks, garage door openers, and voice assistants, enabling builders to offer buyers a holistic smart-home experience that adapts to their lifestyle.


## Partnering for sustainable communities


The builder partnerships Resideo has formed now extend beyond individual products to full-scale smart communities. An example is the[collaboration with Habitat for Humanity of Denver](https://www.resideo.com/us/en/corporate/newsroom/featured-articles/resideo-helps-create-the-next-generation-of-smart-affordable-homes/) , where First Alert and Honeywell Home solutions were integrated throughout the organization’s first smart-home community. By incorporating connected thermostats, water detection technologies, and advanced safety systems, the project illustrates how smart solutions can enhance accessibility and affordability for homeowners at every income level.


Sustainability isn’t reserved for luxury builds; energy-efficient, connected technologies can be both scalable and attainable. Across the industry, builders have an opportunity to take meaningful steps today that deliver smarter, safer homes for the future.


## Integrating smart home technology into energy-efficient design


These smart systems also align directly with the building-science principles championed across the high-performance housing industry. The approach Resideo takes supports the broader goals of the Energy & Environmental Building Alliance (EEBA): resilience, efficiency, and environmental stewardship.


By embedding intelligence into the mechanical systems that drive daily comfort and safety, builders can capture energy savings, minimize waste, and enhance homeowner engagement – all while simplifying compliance with evolving energy codes.


For example:


- Smart thermostats help enable demand-response participation and better HVAC load management.
- Water leak detection systems help prevent resource loss and structural waste.
- Smart smoke and CO alarms help extend equipment life through reduced false alarms and improved reliability.
- Whole-home dehumidification helps maintain balanced indoor humidity, improving comfort, supporting HVAC efficiency, and helping protect homes from excess moisture.


Together, these innovations form a framework for sustainable living that helps both people and the planet.


## The builder’s advantage: Differentiation through energy efficiency


For builders and developers, adopting connected home technologies offers a clear business advantage. Homes that integrate smart thermostats, leak detection, and safety systems can enhance homeowner satisfaction and qualify for insurance incentives, lower utility costs, and improved long-term performance metrics.


Resideo’s scalable approach – backed by the Honeywell Home and First Alert brands – can help builders design homes that meet today’s environmental expectations while remaining adaptable for tomorrow’s technologies. By turning energy efficiency into a practical advantage rather than a compliance checkbox, this approach connects comfort, safety, and efficiency in ways that help shape a new generation of homes that work smarter and deliver long-term value for homeowners.

## Frequently Asked Questions:


**What is “connected comfort,” and why does it matter for builders?**


Connected comfort refers to the integration of HVAC, water detection, and life-safety technologies into a unified smart-home ecosystem. For builders, this approach simplifies energy efficiency, supports indoor air quality (IAQ) and water-management goals, and delivers the modern smart-home experience buyers now expect.


**How do smart thermostats contribute to energy-efficient design?**


Heating and cooling account for roughly half of a home’s energy consumption. Smart thermostats help reduce that load by automatically adjusting temperature based on occupancy, schedules, and IAQ needs. Tools like geofencing, radar-based sensing, and ENERGY STAR®–certified performance can improve HERS scores and long-term energy savings for homeowners.


**Can IAQ features make a measurable difference for homeowners?**


Yes. Thermostats and sensors that monitor humidity, VOCs, and estimated CO₂ levels help identify issues early and allow compatible equipment—such as humidifiers, dehumidifiers, or ventilators—to respond automatically. This supports wellness-focused design and helps builders differentiate homes with comfortable living environments.
